what_happened: In job er96, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The reading had the candidate branch pushed so a CI run on it would save the fingerprint cache entry. The user pointed out that GitHub scopes caches differently. A pull_request run restores caches from its own pull request scope (refs/pull/N/merge) and from the base branch. It does not restore from a plain push run on the head branch. So at the start of verification Athena must open or update the job's pull request, with the candidate as its head, through the same host seam `land` uses. Then the CI run that saves the entry is a pull_request run in that scope, and the landing push (a synchronize event) can reuse it. Opening the pull request must not merge anything, because merging stays with `athena land` after verification passes. A failure to open or update the pull request is non-fatal.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text and the local repo view. It has no step that asks, for each CI cache entry, which ref scope saves it, which event types and scopes can restore it, and what a plain push run can see compared with a pull_request run. The host's cache scoping rules are not in a list the reading must consult. The earlier correction (wrv7) fixed the branch-level rule for this same job family, but the finer rule, that the event type and the pull request merge-ref scope decide visibility, stayed outside the reading. So each correction fixed one case, and the system did not learn to model the cache's scope as a whole.
prevention: Add a short, checked table of CI cache scoping rules to the place the reading stage consults, such as ci-routing section 4.1. It should say: which ref scope and event type saves an entry; which runs can restore it (the same pull request's merge ref and the base branch, not a push run on the head branch); and that only main writes main's shared entries. Make the reading stage list, for every cache or stored CI artifact in a request, the saving run, the restoring run and the scope each uses. Have the critic reject a reading that leaves any of these three unstated. With that, a reading that pushes a bare branch and expects a pull_request run to restore from it would be caught before work starts.
proposed_request: When verification starts for a job, open or update the job's pull request with the candidate as its head, through the same host seam `athena land` uses. Do not only push the branch. This makes the CI run that saves the fingerprint cache entry a pull_request run in that pull request's scope (refs/pull/N/merge), and the landing push (a synchronize event) can restore it. Opening the pull request must not merge anything: merging stays with `athena land` after verification passes. If opening or updating the pull request fails, log it and continue; do not fail the job. Main's shared caches must still be written only from main. Record this scoping rule (a pull_request run restores from its own pull request scope and the base branch, not from a push run on the head branch) in the decision entry and in ci-routing section 4.1. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fake host seam shows that starting verification opens the pull request once, and a second start updates it and does not open a second; (2) a test shows that no merge call is made at that step; (3) a test shows that a seam failure at that step leaves the job running and is logged; (4) a test shows that `athena land` finds the existing pull request and reuses it.
